coverageSpotVerification.detail: tests/coverage.json maps exactly the suite-required assertion set of every milestone (7/22/7/5/6/5/6 for m1/m2/m3/m4/m5/m6/m8), and scripts/acceptance.mjs itself refuses to pass unless the declared list equals the instrument's suite-required set in order and every mapped test name equals the test that declares the assertion; the grader re-derived that set from assertions.json and it matched. Reading every test file confirmed the mapped tests exercise the real observables rather than proxies: m1-a03/a04 assert on the rendered error node in the web UI rather than on an API refusal, m2-a22..a24 really scroll the rendered list and compare it against the API pages, m5-a09 also asserts the negative half of the pinned word-prefix semantics, m6-a13 re-verifies the committed sample log's sha256 inside the test, and m8-a01 compares rendered tiles against the store (the grader independently derived the same six numbers over the custom-client API and they matched). No mapping was found dishonest, so no milestone is adjudicated to capability-failure on that ground. Divergence found between suite and grader: exactly one — m4-a09, where the suite's own test is racy while the assertion's observable holds under grader execution (defect d-01).

defects.summary: The lane's own M4 acceptance test is racy, so the M4 suite receipt is not reproducible. Clicking the bubble's edit affordance pre-fills the composer asynchronously (~140 ms; measured 146/140/139 ms), and the test fills immediately, so the late prefill lands on top of the typed text and the committed body becomes "<original><new>". The bubble still matches on substring and still shows the 'edited' label, so the label assertion passes and the server-content assertion then fails. 4 of 7 grader-executed runs of `npm run acceptance -- --milestone m4` failed, always on this one test; driven with a wait for the prefill the edit path is correct every time.

Live Following-feed projection of a followed user's repost is intermittent: in the grader's own full choreography sweep the harness check `repost-following-feed-surface` failed attempts 1 and 3 and passed only attempt 2, so only the best-of-3 rule carried it.

M2 liveness can stall for tens of seconds under a full sequential sweep. The builder's final `all` choreography run records every one of the nine M2 live checks failing 3/3 attempts, each a 10 s timeout waiting for a freshly composed post to appear in the other client's Global feed, plus a failed M8 Insights refresh. A targeted re-run of `m2,m8` and the grader's own full sweep both passed all checks, so the condition is intermittent rather than systematic — but a green M2 choreography receipt is not reliably reproducible in a single continuous sweep.

The conversation composer's edit prefill is asynchronous (~140 ms): immediately after the edit tap the field is empty and the original text arrives afterwards, so characters typed inside that window end up appended after the original rather than inserted into an already-filled field. Benign for a person — the result is what a pre-filled field would have produced — but it is the root cause of d-01.

O1.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ('M1-M4 solid, later milestones patchy or failed on cap') and the 90 anchor ('every in-scope milestone green, including platform-proof artifacts'), placed closer to 90.
O1.justification: Independent execution passed 100 of the manifest's 119 assertions: 1 fail (m3-a02, DM bubbles render no sender avatar) and 18 not-run (the 9 native-artifact ids m6-a01..a07 / m8-a17 / m8-a18, for which no simulator artifact exists anywhere in the lane, plus all 9 M7 ids, which this run's scope defers to a later fresh session but which applicability.json keeps in O1's denominator). Over the 101 ids this report carries: 84 pass, 1 fail, 16 not-run. Clearly better than the 60 anchor — M1, M2, M4, M5, M6 and M8 are green on the web authoring bar, the suite passes for every milestone, the grader's own full choreography sweep came back green on all seven segments, and the checklist's harder grader-class items (server-side edit-window enforcement on the real clock, disappearing-message expiry with every client closed plus client purge and offline-search purge, view-once asset refusal, delete-time asset revocation, the scheduled digest with correct authorized counts and restart idempotency, and the API.md-only client variation) all passed. Short of 90 on two counts the anchor names explicitly: no native/simulator platform proof exists at all, and M7 was not attempted in this run. Evidence: trace.md §2, §4, §5.

O2.anchorsCited: Between the 60 anchor ('a few medium defects off the happy path') and the 90 anchor ('only cosmetic nits'), placed nearer 90.
O2.justification: Ten defects beyond the checklist, none material: 0 blocker, 0 major, 7 minor, 3 cosmetic. Nothing the grader drove produced a crash, wrong data served to a user, or a broken flow, and all twenty adversarial trust-boundary attempts were correctly refused or returned nothing (trace.md §7), including cross-user DM reads, non-member sends, asset fetches, forged senderId, an overridden viewer, post-removal delivery, revoked tokens across every surface, and edits of tombstones. Better than 60 because there is no medium-or-worse defect in any core flow. Short of 90 because the minors are real rather than cosmetic: the M4 milestone receipt is not reproducible (d-01, 4 of 7 runs fail), live repost projection needed best-of-3 to pass (d-02), a full continuous sweep can stall M2 liveness entirely (d-03), the verified scale artifact was mutated after its conformance receipt so it can no longer be re-verified (d-04), two published degradation rules are never evaluated (d-06), and already-viewed media does not render cold-offline on the one platform where that is observable (d-10). Evidence: trace.md §9.

O4.anchorsCited: Between the 30 anchor ('cold-start offline shows an empty or broken app') and the 60 anchor ('reads work; offline writes lost or mis-ordered, or receipts wrong after flush'); the 90 anchor requires the behaviour 'on the native proof ... including M8's durable-queue restart and multi-device convergence evidence'.
O4.justification: Scored only from the harness's artifacts, as the manifest requires. There is no simulator artifact: every choreography segment summary, the builder's and the grader's own, records ios-simulator-m6 and ios-simulator-m8 as {pass: null, receipt: null, status: 'not-recorded'}, there is no --simulator-status file in the lane, and the only native outputs are the per-milestone iOS Hermes bundle exports under artifacts/, which are build artifacts the brief says cannot support a native claim. Cold-start offline and the durable-queue-across-restart proof were therefore never demonstrated. What the harness's structured receipts do show, on web, is genuine and mechanically checkable: two messages composed offline each exposing a visible 'pending' receipt state, flushing to the recipient in send order on reconnect (352.4 ms) with receipts walking to 'read'; warm-offline search over synced messages returning the expected hit with an offline indicator; cross-device read state clearing on the account's other client (274 ms); and dual-offline convergence in server-arrival order with no loss and no duplicates, receipts advancing afterwards. That is well above the 30 anchor for everything that was observed, and below 60 because the dimension's headline observable — cold-start offline reads — has no evidence in any artifact. The dimension also weighs honesty of the gap between claim and guarantee, and here the lane's receipts state the simulator legs as 'not-recorded' rather than claiming them, which is what holds this at 45 rather than lower. Evidence: trace.md §4.6, §4.8, §5.

O5.bandRationale: First-match in the order 0, 30, 60, 90, 75. The 0 branch does not fire: the invariant manifest conformed at verification time (checkpoint verification at 10% and 50% and the final verification all pass with zero mismatches, with the named O5 fixtures — u0500's 500 follows and 100 conversations, u0005's 5, the celebrity's 900 followers and 200 posts, u0901's exact 5-account following list, and the busy group's 50-member roster and 10,000 messages by full API paging — checked through the app's own query path), and the replay cap was not exhausted (932.17 s of a 14,400 s cap, capFractionUsed 0.0647, capExhausted false, all 167,157 actions settled with 0 failures against the committed scale.log). The 30 branch fires: a degradation rule fails. The celebrity write-path rule — the celebrity's post-create acknowledgement p95 must be <= 3x a 5-follower author's — measures 606.62 ms against 17.34 ms, about 35x the bound. The grader corroborated this structurally without writing to the artifact: the lane declares its Following feed as a read-time view, and the platform materialises it per reader (a followingFeed table keyed by readerId plus a followingWork delivery queue, read by a byReaderTime index in the generated residency plan), so a 900-follower post fans out to ~900 timeline rows on the write path. No probe errored, timed out or OOMed at any checkpoint, and the other seven evaluated rules pass, but band 30 is the first match so the 60/90/75 branches are never reached. Because this wave committed no probe set, the pinned published degradation rules were evaluated against the lane's own recorded k=20-after-3-warm-ups measurements rather than against the wave's rotated probe queries; the failing rule is one of the published ones. Evidence: trace.md §8; receipts/scale-replay-evidence.json, receipts/scale-replay-receipt.json.

notes: probeResults is empty by recorded deviation: no holdout probe set was committed for this wave, so execution-order phase 4 was skipped entirely, wave.probeSetSha256 carries the literal 'none-uncommitted', and no probes were invented. The direct consequence is that O3 records null: applicability.json makes O3 applicable here (M6 green, M1-M5 attempted) but scores it 'from the wave's secret rotated holdout probes only', with anchor probes explicitly non-scoring, so there is no admissible input. The grader's own twenty trust-boundary attempts (trace.md §7, all correctly denied) are reported as O2 input, not as O3. By applicability.json's nullDimensionRule a null dimension means per-dimension scores and efficiency statistics only, no weighted total — consistent with this being an N=1 calibration run rather than a claim-eligible wave. Two further recorded deviations: (1) the grading family has not passed the calibration gate, so calibrationPassed is false and the wave record labels this grade 'uncalibrated-grader'; sameFamilyGraded is false. (2) The frozen report schema only permits the 101 M1-M7 assertion ids (patternProperties ^m[1-7]-a[0-9]{2}$), but all 119 manifest assertions were graded in this one independent session; the 18 M8 results are written to the sibling file grading/m8-assertion-results.json so this report stays schema-valid with exactly those 101 ids and no id is duplicated across the two files. The partition was checked programmatically against the manifest: 101 + 18 = 119, no gaps and no overlaps. Also recorded: the lane wrote no run-record.json, so lane.runRecordPath names the path that would have carried it and O5's inputs were read from receipts/scale-replay-evidence.json and its bound receipt rather than from a record's performanceProbes.o5Inputs. rerunsUsed is capped at 1 by the schema; in fact the m8-a11 sub-check took four attempts, the first three defeated by a grader-side hazard (the platform's in-memory dev clock-advance seam versus its durable schedule bookmark) that trace.md §4.8.1 diagnoses and does not charge to the lane, and the M4 suite was executed seven times to characterise defect d-01 rather than to fish for a pass. The grading session was not contaminated: the lane's diary, essay, final report and run log were never opened and no other lane was touched. Machine load is recorded beside every timing measurement (three lanes share this host); the grader's own full choreography sweep ran at 1-minute load averages between 24.7 and 27.7.
